title: Formal initial exponent diagrams and complementary counts
statement: Let $L$ be a commutative ring and $d\ge0$, and write $L[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]$ for the formal series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. An exponent $\alpha\in\mathbf N^d$ is the first exponent of $F$ if its coefficient is nonzero and every coefficient at an exponent strictly smaller in total-degree lexicographic order vanishes. For an ideal $K$ define $\mathcal N(K)=\{\alpha:\exists F\in K,\ \alpha\text{ is the first exponent of }F\}$. In particular zero series contribute no exponent. Put $H_D(n)=\#\{\alpha\notin D:|\alpha|\le n\}$; the counted set is finite. The truncated quotient is $L[[T]]/(K+(T)^{n+1})$. The extension of $D$ by $r$ free final coordinates is the union of the orthants above the vectors $(\alpha,0)$ for $\alpha\in D$; for an upward-closed $D$ it is $D\times\mathbf N^r$. Ordered vertex families, their generated orthants and quotient supports use [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division].
